# A03 report: profile sync, voice bank, answer bank, company research

Branch `v2-a03-profile`. `npm run typecheck` is clean and `npm run selfcheck` passes
(99 checks, 1 skipped; A03's 44 are in `scripts/checks/a03-profile.ts`).

## Acceptance

- ✅ **The profile refreshes daily without overwriting the owner's manual facts.**
  `syncProfile()` reconciles each source into `profile_facts`: new lines are added,
  vanished lines are deactivated (never deleted), and unchanged lines keep their id
  and date. Manual facts are never touched. A fact the owner hides stays hidden
  through later syncs. Rewording a synced fact creates a manual fact and hides the
  original, so the edit survives. A failing source keeps yesterday's facts. All of
  this is tested. The 06:00 trigger belongs to A08's scheduler, which calls
  `syncProfile()`.
- ✅ **Every fact shows its source in the UI data.** `GET /api/master/facts` returns
  `source` (cv | github | portfolio | linkedin | manual), `sourceRef` (a URL, a CV
  section like `CV: cv.pdf › Backend Developer @ Khan Hardware`, or a LinkedIn
  file), `addedAt`, `active` and `hidden`. A selfcheck asserts that every fact has
  both fields.
- ✅ **Unknown question → owner answers → bank → job re-queued, end to end.**
  `recordUnknown()` → `answerUnknown()` (from the UI route or Telegram) saves the
  answer to the bank. It closes that question and every other open question the new
  answer now resolves (same wording or same meaning). For each one it emits
  `{type:'question.answered', questionId, jobId}`, and it moves each parked job
  (`skipped | needs_you | failed`) back to `selected` once it has no other open
  questions. It is tested through both the function and the HTTP route.
- ✅ **The style fingerprint is computed and exposed to A04.** It is recomputed on
  every voice-bank write and returned by `styleFingerprint()`,
  `loadMasterProfile().style` and `GET /api/master/style`. `fingerprintOf(texts)`
  lets A04 measure its letters the same way.

## What I built

### `server/profile/`
| File | What |
| --- | --- |
| `index.ts` | The contract surface. It keeps the stub names and signatures: `syncProfile`, `loadMasterProfile`, `answerFor`, `recordUnknown`, `styleFingerprint`, `learningSkills`. It also re-exports the wider API listed below. |
| `facts.ts` | The fact store. `reconcileFacts(source, incoming, inScope)` gives deterministic ids (source, kind, context and normalised text). Also hidden facts, manual CRUD, and `factsForPrompt()` (active facts grouped by kind, each with its source). |
| `cv.ts` | Turns a CV into facts deterministically from the `profile` extraction, which is already a faithful transcription: one fact per skill, role, bullet, project, degree, certificate and link. `extractProfile()` now calls `syncCvFacts()` after every upload. |
| `github.ts` | Public REST API through the fetcher, with an optional vault token (`github_token`). Only repos the candidate owns count, and a fork only with 3 or more of their own commits. Up to 12 notable repos (ranked by stars, description, recency and topics) become project facts with links, and their languages become skill facts. READMEs are reduced to prose and mined with `profile_sync`. Results are cached by README hash, so an unchanged repo costs nothing. Summary: languages, topics, stars and commits in the last 90 days. A 401 or 403 rate limit fails only that part. |
| `portfolio.ts` | A same-origin crawl of at most 30 pages (and at most 90 fetches). It honours `robots.txt` (groups and longest match), skips assets, strips tracking parameters, ignores off-site and mailto links, and drops hidden elements, navigation, header and footer before anything reaches Claude. Page facts are cached by page hash. An unreachable page keeps its facts; a page that returns 404 or is no longer linked loses them. |
| `linkedin.ts` | Reads the official data export (zip or a single CSV) for Positions, Education, Skills, Certifications, Projects, Honors, Languages, Publications and Courses. Connections, messages and anything about other people are never read. It has an RFC 4180 CSV parser and a zip-bomb guard. Pasted profile text goes through `profile_sync`. Bureau never logs in to or scrapes LinkedIn. |
| `../ai/profile.ts` (refactored, additive) | Adds `extractFacts(sources, ai)`, which uses task `profile_sync`, the `FACT_EXTRACTOR` prompt and fenced `<source ref>` blocks. A fact survives only if it cites a source we sent **and** passes `isNearVerbatim()`: every number in the claim appears in the source, and at least 85% of its meaningful words do. Fabrications and embellishments are dropped in code, not just by the prompt. |
| `voice.ts` | Voice-bank CRUD, the 8 suggested prompts and the style fingerprint: sentence-length mean and standard deviation, moving-average type-token ratio (window 50), contraction rate (possessives excluded), first-person rate, and the top 8 connectives. |
| `questions.ts` | Question normalisation. It cleans the text (contractions, punctuation, `*`, "(required)") and recognises about 34 intents with slots: the skill in "years of React.js experience" becomes `react`, plus currency and country. Pairs with opposite meanings ("authorised to work *without sponsorship*", "current and expected CTC") deliberately get no intent. It also covers country detection and fuzzy text and content words. |
| `answers.ts` | The answer bank: CRUD, seeding, `answerFor()`, `matchOption()` and job scope. Details are below. |
| `unknown.ts` | `recordUnknown` (deduplicated), `listUnknown` (with job title and company), `answerUnknown` (async), `ignoreUnknown` and `requeueJob`. |
| `learning.ts` | Learning-list CRUD. `learningSkills()` returns only `learning` items. |
| `links.ts` | GitHub, portfolio, LinkedIn and social links: derived from the CV, with owner overrides in settings. Also `githubLogin()`. |
| `master.ts` | `loadMasterProfile()`: null with no CV, and cached on a version key (profile `updated_at`, the profile save counter and this module's write counter) with a 30 s TTL for cross-process writes. It returns a `structuredClone` (the selfcheck asserts 300 calls in under 1.5 s). It includes **active** facts only (the full history is on `/api/master/facts`). |
| `sync.ts` | Runs the `cv`, `github` and `portfolio` parts independently, so concurrent calls share one run. If a CV was uploaded after the profile was last built, it re-extracts that CV. It stores the report (`lastSync()`), logs the run and emits an `activity` event. |
| `fetch.ts`, `ai.ts` | The injectable seams. `Fetcher` defaults to `safeFetch`; `recordedFetcher(dir…)` serves `fixtures/<dir>/index.json`. `AiClient` defaults to `structured`/`research`. |
| `routes.ts` | The UI routes (listed below). |

`services/profileStore.ts` gained only `profileVersion()`, a counter bumped by
`saveProfile`. Every v1 export is unchanged.

### `server/research/`
- `researchCompany(company, domain?, opts?)` keeps the stub signature, with an
  optional third argument `{force, fetcher, ai, now, posting}`. It fetches the
  company's home page plus up to 4 of its own about, engineering, blog or careers
  pages through the fetcher. It then calls `research()` (task `research`, at most
  5 web searches, personal social-media domains blocked) with a strict
  public-business-only system prompt and a news window of the last 6 months. It
  parses the final JSON block and validates it.
- `parse.ts`: `extractJson()` reads a fenced block, or failing that the last
  balanced object. `finalizeBrief()` keeps a claim only if its URL was actually
  read (a web-search result, a fetched page, the company's own domain or the
  posting). It drops news older than 6 months or with a future date. It accepts a
  hiring contact **only** from the posting or the company's own pages, and drops
  invalid items without losing the whole brief. If the answer contains no JSON, a
  structured `research` call restructures the notes, and the result is validated
  the same way.
- Cached in `research_briefs` for 14 days, keyed by normalised company name plus
  domain. "Lumen Pay, Inc." and `www.lumenpay…/careers` hit the same brief. Two
  requests for the same brief in flight share one run.
- `researchForJob(jobId)` uses the registry domain, then the apply URL host (job
  boards and ATS hosts are never treated as company sites), and passes the posting
  so a named hiring manager can be cited.

## API for other agents

```ts
// server/profile/index.ts
syncProfile(opts?): Promise<SyncReport>          // SyncReport ⊇ {added}; opts: {parts?, fetcher?, ai?, now?, reextract?}
loadMasterProfile(): MasterProfile | null         // cheap; active facts only
answerFor(question, {jobId?, fieldKind?, options?}): Promise<Answered|null>   // with options, value is one of them or null
recordUnknown({question, jobId, fieldKind, options?}): string
answerUnknown(id, {answer, scope?, question?}): Promise<{entry, answered[], requeued[]}>   // A08 Telegram /answer
ignoreUnknown(id), listUnknown(status), requeueJob(jobId)
styleFingerprint(): StyleFingerprint | null;  fingerprintOf(texts[]): StyleFingerprint      // A04 lint
learningSkills(): string[];  factsForPrompt(facts?): string;  listVoice();  matchOption(value, options)
normalizeQuestion(q), detectIntent(q), listAnswers(), upsertAnswer(...), lastSync(), invalidateMasterProfile()
// server/research/index.ts
researchCompany(company, domain?, opts?): Promise<ResearchBrief>;  researchForJob(jobId, opts?);  cachedBrief(company, domain?)
```

**`answerFor` resolution order:**
1. An exact normalised question, or the same intent with a compatible slot. The
   most specific scope wins, then owner answers over derived ones. Confidence is
   0.97 for exact, 0.92 for intent, and 0.08 lower for derived answers.
2. The profile itself: LinkedIn, GitHub and portfolio links, location, name, email,
   phone, and overall years of experience.
3. Fuzzy matching, only between questions with no recognised intent. It needs both
   embedding cosine and content-word overlap: hash 0.55/0.5, MiniLM 0.8/0.34.
   Confidence is 0.72 to 0.92.

Scope covers country (from the job's location or the question's own text, so
"right to work in the UK" scopes itself), job type
(full-time/contract/internship/part-time/remote/onsite/hybrid) and ATS. If a
stored answer can't honestly map onto the field's options, `answerFor` returns
null. Yes/no answers, numeric ranges ("3" → "2-3 years"), containment and word
overlap all count as mappings.

**Seeding:** 28 common questions are added as empty placeholders for the owner to
fill, plus "years of experience with X" for the top 6 core skills. Answers are also
derived from the v1 preferences: notice period, salary expectation, relocation,
remote-only → onsite, and the `Q:/A:` and `Question? answer` lines in
`extraAnswers`. Sponsorship is derived only once the owner has filled
`workAuthorization`, never from the default `false`, because it is a legal
attestation. Owner answers always beat derived ones, and a seed the owner deletes
stays deleted.

## How to run and test

- `npm run selfcheck -- a03` runs only the A03 checks (offline, replay mode, hash
  embeddings).
- The checks use fixtures: `fixtures/github/`, `fixtures/portfolio/`,
  `fixtures/research/` and `fixtures/linkedin/` (each has a README), plus
  `fixtures/claude/profile_sync/*.json` (3 recordings) and
  `fixtures/claude/research/*.json` (1). Each recording includes deliberately
  fabricated or unsourced claims that the code must reject.
- The recordings are generated by `npx tsx scripts/a03/record-fixtures.ts` (add
  `--preview` to print what each call sends). The inputs are fixed in
  `scripts/a03/scenario.ts`, with the clock at 2026-11-01. **Re-run it after
  changing `FACT_EXTRACTOR`, `RESEARCH_SYSTEM`, the prompt builders or a fixture
  page**, otherwise replay fails with `REPLAY_MISSING` and the hash.
- What the tests cover: the CV sync diff (new CV adds facts, removed bullets
  deactivate, manual and hidden facts survive, owner rewording), 20 answer-bank
  paraphrases plus 6 negatives, option mapping and scope, profile answers, intent
  conflicts, unknown → answer → bank → re-queue (several questions and several
  jobs, mid-flight jobs left alone, event emitted), the GitHub rules (forks,
  notability, README guard, rate limit, cache), the crawler (robots, assets, 404,
  hidden injection, cache), LinkedIn (zip, single CSV, paste), the full sync with
  one part failing, the fingerprint maths, the learning list, research
  (parse, sources, 6-month window, hiring contact, cache, fallback JSON) and the
  routes via `inject`.
- I also smoke-tested the real server: started with a temp `BUREAU_DATA_DIR`,
  calling `/api/master*` with a session and CSRF token worked, and there are no
  route collisions.

## Known limits

- **MiniLM thresholds are not measured.** The fuzzy thresholds for the real
  embedding model (cosine ≥ 0.8, word overlap ≥ 0.34) are conservative guesses; the
  tests run on the hash fallback. Most real-world matching goes through intents,
  which don't depend on embeddings. Fuzzy matching is deliberately strict: a
  missed match becomes a question for the owner, while a wrong match becomes a
  wrong answer on a real application.
- **CV re-extraction is not covered by the selfcheck.** The path that re-extracts a
  CV uploaded since the last build calls the v1 `profile` task. It needs a real CV
  plus a recording, and A11's seeded profile is the natural place for that. The
  diff logic it feeds is tested.
- **JavaScript-rendered portfolios yield little.** The crawler reads server-rendered
  HTML only. A portfolio built as a pure client-side app gives almost no text,
  which shows in the sync report as a low fact count.
- **GitHub coverage is capped.** It reads up to 12 notable repos and checks up to 5
  forks per sync, to stay inside the unauthenticated limit of 60 requests an hour.
  A token raises the limit but not the caps.
- **LinkedIn pasted text depends on Claude.** Text in a language other than English
  may fail the verbatim guard more often, because the guard is token-based.
- **Concurrent syncs share options.** `syncProfile()` calls that overlap share the
  first call's options, so a "Sync now" during the 06:00 run returns that run's
  report.
- **Research quality is only known offline.** Only the parser and validation are
  tested; the live web-search quality is not. A brief whose sources fail
  validation can come back thin rather than wrong, by design.
- **GitHub summary extras are stripped on re-parse.** `MasterProfile.github`
  carries extra fields (`recentCommits`, `archived`, `profileUrl`) that are not in
  the contract yet, so anything that parses the profile with `MasterProfileSchema`
  removes them. See `docs/build/requests/A03.md`.

## Follow-ups for other agents

- **A08:** call `syncProfile()` at 06:00 local time. The `question.answered` event
  arrives after A03 has already moved the parked job to `selected`; A08 only needs
  to schedule it. Telegram `/answer <id> <text>` should call
  `await answerUnknown(id, {answer: text})`. The digest can list
  `listUnknown('open')`.
- **A05 / A07:** `answerFor(question, {jobId, fieldKind, options})`, then
  `recordUnknown(...)` when the result is null or below 0.7. Pass `options` so the
  value comes back as an exact option.
- **A04:** read `loadMasterProfile()` for `facts` (each with source), `voiceBank`
  and `style`. Use `fingerprintOf([letter])` for the lint, `learningSkills()` for
  "Currently learning", `factsForPrompt()` for a stable prompt block, and
  `researchForJob(jobId)` or `researchCompany()` for hooks (every claim has a
  `sourceUrl`).
- **A10:** the routes above. The onboarding "GitHub sync preview" can be
  `PUT /api/master/links` then `POST /api/master/sync {parts:['github']}` then
  `GET /api/master/github`.
- **A11:** `recordedFetcher()` and the four fixture folders are ready for e2e. The
  recorder shows how to make more recordings without an API key.
- **Lead:** the contract requests are in `docs/build/requests/A03.md`. They are
  optional and nothing is blocked on them.
